imageAlt: Teen golfer about to play a ball outside a marked relief area on the fairway.

issues: Yellow marking is a curved arc instead of a clearly defined shape for a relief area.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Clarify the yellow marking as a realistic, closed, defined relief area boundary instead of a simple arc or curve.

questions.title: What happens if you play from the wrong spot after a drop?
questions.question: You need to drop your ball in the right place to keep playing. If you drop your ball in the wrong place and hit it from there, what happens?

choices.text: Nothing happens, you can keep playing.
You stop playing in the game.

questions.explanation: If you drop your ball in the wrong place and then hit it, you get 2 extra shots added to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When you let go of the ball from your knee to put it back in play.
The special spot where you must drop your ball.

questions.teachingTip: Show the difference between a correct and incorrect drop area using cones or markers, and have children practise dropping balls in the right spot.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think a drop can be made anywhere on the course.
They might believe the penalty is less than 2 strokes, or not know there is a penalty.

questions.title: Penalty for Playing from the Wrong Spot After a Drop
questions.question: If you drop your ball outside the relief area and then play it from there, what penalty do you receive?
questions.explanation: There is a two-stroke penalty for playing a ball from the wrong place after a drop, according to the Rules of Golf.
